name: Shillong
description: Capital city and district headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. Hill station with colonial architecture, lakes, markets, and vibrant Khasi culture.

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest peak in Meghalaya at approximately 1,965 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong city, surrounding hills, and Bangladesh plains. Sacred site for Khasi people.
facts: IAF radar station nearby; photo ID required
Best views in clear weather Oct-Mar

name: Elephant Falls
description: Multi-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, originally named Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Accessible with steps and surrounded by ferns and greenery.
facts: Named after a rock formation destroyed in 1897 earthquake

name: Ward's Lake
description: Man-made lake in central Shillong named after Sir William Ward. Popular for boating, walking paths, gardens, and as a city hangout.

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Museum and research centre showcasing the cultural heritage of North East India's indigenous peoples through galleries, artefacts, and a skywalk.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Famous hill station once considered the wettest place on Earth. Gateway to waterfalls, caves, living root bridges, and dramatic limestone landscapes.
facts: Base for Nohkalikai and root bridge treks

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 metres, cascading into a turquoise pool near Sohra. Iconic and culturally significant.

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented multi-stream waterfall dropping over 300 metres near Sohra, also known as Seven Sisters Falls. Spectacular during monsoon.

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible lit limestone cave near Sohra with stalactites, fossils, and short walkable route suitable for beginners.
facts: Part of Meghalaya's extensive cave systems

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Unique two-tier living root bridge grown from Ficus elastica roots by Khasi communities over generations in Nongriat village. Requires a steep trek of ~3500 steps from Tyrna.

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Known as Asia's Cleanest Village. Offbeat Khasi village near the Bangladesh border with living root bridges nearby, skywalk, and community eco-tourism.

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon and viewpoint near Smit offering sweeping views of valleys, hills, and rivers. Popular for photography and short treks.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove preserved by Khasi communities, rich in biodiversity, medicinal plants, and traditional ecological knowledge. Guided nature walks available.

name: Arwah Cave
description: Lit cave near Sohra famous for prehistoric marine fossils visible in the limestone walls. Accessible with short forest walk.
